entries.meaning: The energy transferred when a force moves its object, calculated as force times distance in the force's direction, measured in joules.
entries.example: A force of 50 N pushes a crate 4 m. Work = force x distance = 50 x 4 = 200 J. Check the units: newtons times metres gives joules, and doing the same 200 J in 2 s instead of 10 s raises the power from 20 W to 100 W without changing the work.

entries.meaning: How fast work is done, calculated as work divided by time, measured in watts: the same 200 J in 2 s is 100 W, in 10 s only 20 W.
entries.example: Work: a 50-newton force pushes a crate 4 metres, so the work done is 50 times 4 = 200 joules - and with no movement the distance is zero, so no work is done at all.

entries.meaning: What work transfers between stores and forms - it is never created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another.
entries.example: Power: the same 200 joules done in 10 seconds gives 20 watts; done in 2 seconds it gives 100 watts - same work, less time, more power.

entries.meaning: The energy a raised mass stores because of its height, calculated as mass times g times height: 2 kg at 5 m stores 98 J.
entries.example: Conservation in a fall: a 2-kilogram mass 5 metres up holds 98 joules of GPE; as it falls the GPE drains into KE, and just before landing all 98 joules are kinetic - the total stays 98 joules throughout.

entries.meaning: The energy a moving object has because of its motion - the form GPE becomes as a mass falls.
entries.example: Check the thinking: the car's chemical energy becomes kinetic energy plus heat, so when the petrol runs out the car stops - but the energy has changed form, not vanished.

entries.meaning: The unit of work and energy: one joule is the work done when a force of one newton moves its object one metre.
entries.example: Calculate work as force times distance, and say why no movement means no work

entries.meaning: The unit of power: one watt is one joule of work done every second.
entries.example: Calculate power as work divided by time and compare powers for the same work done at different speeds
